0009990001.body: Item 2.06 Material Impairments. On October 14, 2026, the Board of Directors of Litware concluded that a non-cash impairment charge of $2.0 billion is required for the goodwill of its hardware business. The charge will reduce the company's operating income for the third quarter by 15%.

Item 2.06 Material Impairments. On October 14, 2026, Litware concluded that an impairment charge is required for certain long-lived assets of its consumer software business. The company has not yet determined the amount of the charge. The impairment could have a material adverse effect on the company's results of operations.

Item 8.01 Other Events. Litware updated its investor presentation, which is posted on its website. The risk factors in the presentation state that if a key supplier were to file for bankruptcy, the company's production could be disrupted.

Item 8.01 Other Events. Litware completed a review of how it records revenue. The review found no errors that would cause the company's previously issued financial statements to no longer be reliable.
Item 1.01 Entry into a Material Definitive Agreement. On October 14, 2026, Litware entered into an agreement with a payments company to form a joint venture that will launch a mobile payments app.

Item 5.02 Departure of Directors or Certain Officers; Compensatory Arrangements of Certain Officers. This Amendment No. 1 amends the report filed on October 1, 2026 only to report the compensation of the company's new Chief Financial Officer, who will receive an annual base salary of $750,000.

Item 8.01 Other Events. On October 14, 2026, Litware completed its offering of $1.5 billion of senior notes. Item 9.01 Financial Statements and Exhibits. Exhibit 5.1 Opinion of Adatum Legal LLP: In our opinion, the notes have been duly authorized and are valid and binding obligations of the company.
Item 8.01 Other Events. On October 14, 2026, Litware announced a new cloud storage product for small businesses. The company expects the product to double its cloud revenue.
